items.title: Billions in cash can't be accounted for. Where is it all going?
items.description: There is no shortage of theories, from stacks of cash hidden at home to illicit activities, but little in the way of definitive answers.

items.title: PM apologises for saying he would shag Kylie Minogue during podcast game
items.description: Anthony Albanese made the comments during a game of "shag, marry, date" on the Bush Deep podcast on Friday, which have been widely condemned as inappropriate.

items.title: Call for investigation into cricket pitches on ovals after football tragedy
items.description: Nathan Fitzgerald's club has asked authorities to look at the way hard cricket pitches are covered on multi-use ovals as the 27-year-old continues to receive end-of-life care.

items.title: Breaking: Cannibalism probe in 4yo's death on NSW Central Coast
items.description: Police sources confirm to the ABC that cannibalism will form part of an investigation into the death of a four-year-old boy on the New South Wales Central Coast.

items.title: Belgium slams FIFA decision after Trump intervenes on US star's behalf
items.description: US striker Folarin Balogun is free to play Belgium despite earning a red card in his last match, in a shock decision that delights Donald Trump and "astonishes" the Belgians.

items.title: Live: Haaland double delivers Norway win over Brazil, England match delayed by storms
items.description: Two goals from Erling Haaland deliver Norway an upset win over Brazil in New Jersey, before Mexico hosts England at the Azteca. Follow live.

items.title: The world is getting pure Trump and the US presidency may never be the same
items.description: Donald Trump is undertaking regime change, not just in Venezuela, but on US soil and it is unlikely the presidency will ever be the same.

items.title: Live: Australia strikes new defence alliance with Fiji
items.description: Australia strikes a new defence alliance with Fiji on top of the Vuvale Union treaty. Follow live.

items.title: What household debt levels tell us about the rise of One Nation
items.description: The paradox of a strong economy and stock market with very low consumer sentiment is not close to being resolved. Quite the opposite, the disconnect is, if anything, widening.

items.title: As its people dig, suspicion distracts Venezuela's government
items.description: Instead of focusing all its efforts on coordinating a widescale rescue operation, the Venezuelan government has been accused of hindering the response, and as has become apparent, our ability to cover it.

items.title: Safety fears spark calls for better protections for Neil the seal
items.description: The elephant seal has been attracting onlookers in southern Tasmania as well as a growing social media audience. But fears for his wellbeing, and concerns that some people aren't keeping their distance, have led to calls to better protect Neil.

items.title: The 'dirty little secret' in active funds management and ETFs boom
items.description: A record number of exchange traded funds were added to the Australian share market in the past financial year.

items.title: Live: ASX set to slip despite strength in global markets
items.description: The ASX looks likely to open lower despite the Gulf cease fire holding and a positive sentiment on global markets. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: From Call of Duty to Dreamtime: These designers are lighting up video games
items.description: As part of NAIDOC Week, we meet the Indigenous creatives who are re-shaping Australia's video game industry.

items.title: Is a full day of screen time for kids ever OK?
items.description: Screen time has become a phrase that makes "parents feel instantly guilty", but how detrimental is a full day of screens on the odd occasion, like during school holidays or when you are home sick?

items.title: History quiz: Tackle our questions on Harry Potter, space stations and more
items.description: Let us test your smarts about Captain James Cook's last voyage, the debut release of a popular British girl group and other historical events.

items.title: 'Oldest continually practised medicine' being passed on to students
items.description: Aboriginal Australians have used native plants as bush medicine for tens of thousands of years. On Larrakia land, medical students are learning how nature can heal.

items.title: Experts and union warn about ABC's AI use
items.description: Experts and the journalists’ union have welcomed the ABC’s plans to use artificial intelligence responsibly, but warned misuse could damage trust in the public broadcaster.

items.title: Fears for imprisoned Gaza doctor Hussam Abu Safiya
items.description: Hussam Abu Safiya's lawyers believe he is at risk of being killed behind bars in an Israeli prison.

items.title: 'Truly special': Australia wins T20 World Cup by downing England in final
items.description: Australia has won the ICC Women's T20 World Cup in commanding style, defeating England by seven wickets in the final at Lord's.

items.title: AFP to push Australia's policing model to UN
items.description: The AFP commissioner will promote Pacific police training as a model for the United Nations when she addresses police delegates from 140 nations this week.

items.title: First Nations commissioner warns against Queensland adoption push
items.description: Australia's Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children commissioner has warned Queensland's push to increase adoptions could disproportionately affect First Nations children and risk repeating the harms of past forced child removals.

items.title: Fire damage to 10 shops after arson ram raid in Melbourne
items.description: More than 80 firefighters are at the scene in Richmond, where 10 businesses are burning after a shop was rammed and set alight this morning.

items.title: Sabalenka to 'get drunk and forget about tennis' after Wimbledon exit
items.description: Naomi Osaka downs top seed Aryna Sabalenka in straight sets in a fourth round meeting of grand slam champions at Wimbledon.

items.title: Djokovic overcomes 'meltdowns' to topple Federer's Wimbledon record
items.description: Novak Djokovic fights off a plucky opponent and his own demons to etch his name into another corner of the record books at Wimbledon.
